There is no catch.

alltheplugins.com is an open-source collection of audio plugins that anybody can use to express their musical creativity. No subscriptions, sign-ups, or payment needed. If you want, you can buy me a coffee to support the site, but it’s also cool if you don’t.

I’m a musician, and this is a personal, noncommercial project.

Want to contribute? If you make music, try the plugins and share your feedback. If you build plugins, share something you’ve made. If you have an eye for design, help make the plugins look as good as they sound. If you’re good at explaining things, help me improve the instructions.

And of course, sharing alltheplugins.com with your friends helps too. Contribute

    About the project

    Made for music.
    Shared freely.

    Independent audio plugins, built by a musician and shared with anyone who wants to create.

    Why I’m sharing these plugins

    I’m a musician building a collection of free audio plugins. They’re available for anyone to use in their own music and share with others.

    This is a personal, noncommercial project.

    Free to use.

    Your creativity should not be locked behind a paywall. I want to put creative tools in your hands so you can make music, express yourself, and create human art without the cost of entry.

    Make it yours.

    My MIT-licensed plugin binaries come with broad permissions to use, modify, and share. Each plugin page includes its full license and required notices.

    Pass it on.

    Modify a plugin to match your workflow, or mix and match to spark new ideas. Share what you make and contribute through the project repository.

    A few practical details

    Getting started

    Each plugin page lists its downloads, specific requirements, controls, and installation instructions. Choose the download for your operating system and plugin format.

    About the inspirations

    My plugins are inspired by sounds and workflows I’ve encountered in my 20+ years as a music producer and mix engineer. All my plugins are original software, inspired by familiar sounds to enable your creativity. I have no affiliation with the vendors of products that inspire them.

    Help the project

    Contribute

    Support the project, share a plugin, or help make the collection more useful. You don’t need to write code to contribute.

    Support the project

    If these plugins are useful to you, you can leave an optional tip. The plugins remain free to download and use.

    Support on Ko-fi

    Contribute a plugin

    Made an audio plugin you’d like to share? Submit your project for consideration.

    • A project or source-code link, with a license that permits sharing and any required third-party notices.
    • A short description, an actual editor screenshot, and installation and usage instructions.
    • Available builds and formats, such as Windows VST3, Mac VST3, or Mac AU, and what you’ve tested.

    Submit work you created or have permission to share. Submissions are reviewed for licensing, functionality, and compatibility before being added to the collection.

    Submit a plugin on GitHub

    Report a problem or suggest an improvement

    Tell me which plugin you’re using, what happened, and how to reproduce it. Ideas for clearer controls, better documentation, or useful features are welcome too.

    Share feedback on GitHub

    Help with plugin UI design

    If you have an eye for design, help make the plugins look as good as they sound. Layout, typography, clearer controls, and original artwork can all make a difference. Share a mockup or suggest improvements to an existing plugin.

    Offer design help on GitHub

    Help test or improve documentation

    Try a plugin in your music-making workflow, help explain a control, or suggest a correction to its instructions. Small improvements help other musicians get started.

    Offer to help on GitHub

    Privacy

    This site uses Google Analytics to measure visits and plugin download-button activations.

    Analytics collection starts by default. Download counts record button activations, not completed transfers. Reports include the public plugin name, platform, format and canonical page. Google receives usage and browser/device information, with cookies or similar identifiers where applicable.

    This measurement does not use advertising features or ad personalization.

    You can manage cookies in your browser (Chrome instructions), read how Google uses information, or review the Google Analytics opt-out add-on.
